title: Unit 42 describes Com-affiliated vishing campaigns stealing data from financial, healthcare and legal firms
date_note: Date of Unit 42's report; the activity it describes runs since August 2026.

key_findings: Com-affiliated actors are running repeated vishing-led data theft and extortion waves against financial services, healthcare and legal organizations, mainly in the U.S., UK and Australia.

Callers pose as IT support and send employees to tailored adversary-in-the-middle phishing pages that capture credentials and MFA approvals, after which the attackers enroll their own MFA devices within minutes.
A newly described cluster, CL-CRI-1264, mainly targets healthcare and pharma and has used personal mobile devices as well as corporate workstations.
A malicious Chrome-impersonating browser extension, sideloaded in Developer Mode, adds keylogging, cookie theft and a DevTools-based remote control module.
Australian targeting rose from under 1% of observed subdomains in August and September to about 13% in October, making it the second most-targeted country.
recommendations: Move to phishing-resistant MFA such as FIDO2 or passkeys.

place: United States (report's most-affected country; no single victim location)
geo_basis: country named by the report as mainly affected
summary: Unit 42 attributes vishing-led data theft and extortion since August 2026 to Com-affiliated actors, mostly against financial services, healthcare and legal organisations in the U.S., UK and Australia. Callers pose as IT staff; in one cluster, phishing servers relayed credentials and MFA approvals in real time and an unauthorized MFA device was enrolled within minutes of authenticating. Unit 42 says they occasionally exfiltrated tens of millions of CRM and recruiting records.
plain: Palo Alto's Unit 42 says criminals phone staff pretending to be IT help desks, trick them past multi-factor login, then steal data and demand payment.
exec: Help-desk phone scams are defeating MFA at financial, healthcare and legal firms, leading to large data theft and extortion.
action: Per Unit 42: tighten help desk verification, move to phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/passkeys), use browser extension allowlists, gain visibility into identity actions and alert on unauthorized data exports.
impact: Unit 42 says some intrusions exfiltrated tens of millions of CRM and recruiting records; no victims are named.

validation.note: Vendor research report by Unit 42 (primary); no second publisher read.

review.note: Compared title, date, sectors, countries, since August 2026, tens of millions CRM and recruiting records, CL-CRI-1264 relay and MFA enrolment, Australia under 1% to about 13%, Microsoft 365 and recommendations against the Unit 42 report; single_source primary is right.
